title: NGTM: Substructure-based Neural Graph Topic Model for Interpretable Graph Generation
subcategory: topic modelling transferred to graphs (substructure topics)
problem: Graph generators are realistic but opaque about why structures are produced.
architecture: Graphs are mixtures of latent topics, each a Gaussian over latent embeddings of substructures learned with a conditional VAE; a topic-proportion vector (softmax of a Gaussian) selects topics for W substructures, which are decoded and sequentially assembled under a global structural variable using GCN encoders and attention-based mapping matrices.
metrics: MMD of degree, clustering, orbit, spectral and diameter statistics
key_results: MUTAG: average MMD 0.053 and F1 98.72, best among generators; Lobster F1 100.
Ogbg-molbbbp: lowest average MMD (0.032) but F1 96.38 vs 96.85 for G2PT.
strengths: Brings topic-model interpretability (topic mixtures over substructures) to graph generation.
Topic-level control of graph properties (e.g. diameter, carcinogenicity class).

limitations.text: Hyper-parameters (K = 10, W = 30) chosen to balance interpretability and quality rather than for best accuracy.
Not best on all datasets/metrics (e.g. F1 on Ogbg-molbbbp).

notes: Included as an example of topic modelling beyond text.
